string.name: whats_new_content
string.translation_description: HTML content listing new features in this release, shown in the What's new dialog and appended to the Help screen. Please do not change the < and > markup.

resources.string:
BepiColombo: a new look, and the sky through your camera

Try the new graphics engine (beta)

A more realistic daytime and twilight sky, clearer labels, and a subtle underline on objects that have an info card. It is on by default in this beta. You can switch between Enhanced and Classic any time under Settings → Appearance → Graphics engine. We would love to hear how it works on your phone.

Through-camera mode (beta)

See the sky drawn over your phone\'s live camera image. Turn on Through-camera mode in the Layers sheet, or with the camera button on the layer rail. It is very experimental, and we are still deciding which exposure controls make sense, so tell us what you would want to adjust. A Night photo switch in the camera panel takes a longer exposure for dim skies, on phones that support it. Tap the shutter button to share what you see.

Handier layer buttons

The sky colouring and through-camera buttons now sit on the layer rail. The grid and horizon have moved to the Layers sheet.

Smarter search

An exact name match now comes first, and you can find Orion\'s Belt, the Small Dipper and Tres Marias by name.

Support screen

The Support screen now asks for a store review, and its rows look tappable.

Tonight sheet

A new Tonight sheet gathers what is worth seeing right now — the Moon, visible planets, and any meteor shower or satellite pass coming up.

New objects

Search now finds TON 618, one of the most massive black holes known, and info cards for Voyager 1, Voyager 2 and BepiColombo. An Info button in search jumps straight to an object\'s card.

Satellites are coming back

Satellites are returning in a gradual rollout, so you may not see them yet.

Recently, in Cassini

  • Satellites: switch on the Satellites layer to find the ISS and Tiangong, and tap one for its next visible passes. Satellites are being rolled out gradually to protect the server, so you may not see them yet.
  • Plan your night: info cards show live facts and an Upcoming section for the Moon, planets and meteor showers.
  • Grid and widget: choose how bright the grid lines are, and use the new compact 1x1 Moon phase widget.
  • Better search: find asterisms such as the Big Dipper, and Earth.

And this is just the start...

We have many long asked-for features coming very soon.

About the release name

BepiColombo is the ESA/JAXA spacecraft that reached Mercury in November 2026, after an eight-year journey, to study the planet closest to the Sun.

string.name: whats_new_content_ios
string.translation_description: HTML content for the iPhone release, shown in the What's new screen and the post-update dialog in place of the longer release notes of earlier versions. Please do not change the < and > markup.

resources.string:
What\'s new on iPhone and iPad

  • Notifications: optional alerts for meteor shower peaks, lunar eclipses and a summary of tonight\'s sky, at most one a day. Everything is off until you turn it on under Settings → Notifications.
  • iPad: Sky Map now fills larger screens and works in every orientation.
  • Satellites: see the International Space Station and other satellites crossing the sky. Satellites are being rolled out gradually to protect the server, so you may not see them yet.
  • Support screen: tell a friend about Sky Map, or rate it.

And this is just the start...

More is on the way. Tell us what you would like from the Support screen.

string.name: beta_user_help_text
string.translation_description: Usually-empty HTML content shown to beta testers asking for feedback, appended in the What's new dialog and the Help screen. Please do not change the < and > markup.

resources.string:
Thanks for testing!

Please try the new Graphics engine. It is on by default in this beta (Enhanced under Settings). It draws a more realistic daytime and twilight sky and clearer labels. Tell us if anything looks wrong, especially a black or garbled sky.

Then try through-camera (AR) mode. Turn on Through-camera mode in the Layers sheet to see the sky over the live camera image. It is still very experimental, and we are still deciding which exposure controls make sense, so we would love to hear what you would want to adjust.

You can also share what you see from the overflow menu, or with the shutter in AR mode.

Send feedback from the Support screen.
